To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

ductal lavage (DL) fluid from women at high risk for breast cancer contains cells that are abnormal in their nuclear DNA content, in their morphology, and in their expression of cell-cycle-related proteins.

nipple aspiration and ductal lavage (NAL) are safe and effective methods for sampling breast ducts, and that nipple aspiration and lavaged fluid cytology (NAC and NALC, respectively) can detect breast cancer in situ and in the early stages of invasion.

(1) nipple aspiration is a safe and feasible technique for the evaluation of women with a family history of breast cancer, (2) nipple aspiration fluid contains epithelial cells that have a similar morphology to ductal lavage cells, (3) the cytologic evaluation of nipple aspiration fluid is a useful adjunct to mammographic screening in the evaluation of women at high risk for breast cancer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of novel, non-invasive, and minimally invasive technologies for breast cancer screening, diagnosis, and treatment.
the development and validation of a noninvasive technique to screen for breast cancer and the identification of the most effective and least toxic treatments for breast cancer.
the development of novel, effective, and safe therapeutic strategies against cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the evidence for the use of ductal lavage and nipple aspiration in the screening and early detection of breast cancer is insufficient.
the evidence to date is insufficient to recommend the use of ductal lavage for breast cancer screening in women who are not at increased risk for breast cancer.
the intraductal techniques are not ready for routine clinical use.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
these techniques have the potential to be a powerful tool for the early detection of breast cancer, especially in women at high risk.
ductoscopy is the most invasive and expensive of the 3 techniques and has the least amount of data supporting its use.
ductal lavage is a safe, simple and effective method for sampling the ductal system of the breast and can be used to identify patients who are at increased risk of developing breast cancer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nipple aspirate fluid and ductal lavage are both feasible and safe in the clinical setting, and that nipple aspirate and ductal lavages can be obtained from most women.
ductal lavage is a safe and well tolerated procedure.
ductal lavage and aspiration can provide a window into the breast that can be used for both research and clinical purposes.
